We've had voice agents for a while. Now they've gotten a lot better.

For a long time, voice AI was good at conversation and not much else. It could answer questions and take a message, but anything that touched a real system ended with "let me have someone follow up."

What changed is real-time tool calling. The models have been smart enough to pick the right tool and use it in the middle of a live call, fast enough that the guest never feels a long pause. 

And with our hospitality MCPs, our voice agent can take a booking in your PMS, change a reservation, or reset a door code, on the call, without a handoff.

For our initial group of users, voice resolution went from 56% to 92%. That is the share of calls the agent finishes on its own, no callback, no human handoff.

AI agents that elevate the guest experience requires the work to be done while the guest is still on the line.

Guests in LatAm send 2x more messages than in North America.

We looked at millions of guest messages on Conduit and ave…

detail_evidence.source_text:
Punn Kam

Promoted by Conduit

Guests in LatAm send 2x more messages than in North America.

We looked at millions of guest messages on Conduit and averaged them by property. The spread was not what I expected.

Messages per property per month:

- Latin America: 23.7
- Middle East and Africa: 21.5
- Europe: 19.0
- Asia-Pacific: 15.4
- North America: 10.3

Latin America runs more than double North America. Inside the regions it gets wider still, with Argentina at 52.5 and Brazil at 43.1 against Australia at 10.4 and the United States at 9.6.

I don't think there's a single cause. North America may be more established with self-check-ins, which reduce message volume. The density of Latin America might make navigation more confusing. 

Whatever the reason, operators must staff up for the demand across both the average and on seasonal peaks. AI agents must play a major role in that staffing plan.

Full analysis in the comments.

Today we're launching Portals, the biggest release in Conduit's history.

Portals is one link for everything a guest needs. Check-in, upsells, payments, and a chat agent built in that answers their questions and books the upsells itself.

Here's the flow:

1. A guest books a stay and gets texted their portal link
2. They verify with a selfie against their ID
3. They sign the check-in waiver
4. Their room key drops into their wallet, and they land in their portal: custom upsell offers and every detail of the stay in one place

Then it's check-in day. They show up, walk to the room, and swipe to open. If the room is already cleaned, an early check-in offer pops up: get in now for $40. 

Land somewhere before 1pm and you're buying that every time. And it's easy money the hotel used to leave on the table.

If you're already on Conduit, it's live in your sidebar right now.

If you're not yet, change that by clicking the link in the comments to talk to our team. 

Btw, if these don't pay for themselves, you don't pay for it!

commentary.text: Francesco Taiano runs short-term rentals across Italy and Dubai. In one year, upsells alone reached 5% of his Dubai reve…

detail_evidence.source_text:
Cole Rubin

Promoted by Conduit

Francesco Taiano runs short-term rentals across Italy and Dubai. In one year, upsells alone reached 5% of his Dubai revenue. Here's how he did it:

Initially, his team was spending most of the day answering the same guest questions over and over, then re-answering them in a different language. 

On top of that, 50 to 70% of the maintenance issues guests reported were things they could've fixed themselves in two minutes, if someone had just walked them through it. 

To keep up with the volume, he was running virtual assistant teams out of the Philippines and Pakistan just to cover the messages, a workaround that kept things running but didn't let the business grow.

So he moved the whole operation onto Conduit and built custom tooling on top of it: 

- A smart-lock integration for guest check-in
- Automated payment links
- A knowledge base he manages himself

As a result:

→ Guests now get instant answers in their own language, and the agent walks them through minor maintenance fixes on the spot
→ Positive reviews went up over the year, because guests get help the moment they need it instead of waiting on a VA at 2am
→ The same internal team now covers both Italy and Dubai, freed up for sales and new business, with no new hires

Instead of shrinking his team, Francesco used AI to let them do more, and stopped needing outside help just to keep the lights on.

--

We wrote a breakdown of how Francesco built this out, including the custom tooling behind it and exactly how the upsell automation escalates offers straight to the provider.

detail_evidence.source_text:
Punn Kam

Promoted by Conduit

A boutique hotel upsold me before I ever set foot in the building.

24 hours before check-in, instead of the usual "Dear guest, your check-in instructions are attached" email, they texted me a link.

I opened it on my phone: directions from the airport, my room details, the wifi password. While I was poking around, an early check-in and a massage showed up on the front page, and I bought them with Apple Pay, all before I left for my flight.

Then, the moment I landed, I received another text: "Hi Punn, we have a discounted upgrade on the Corner King room you stayed in last time. Let me know if you'd like it. The offer's also in your portal." I thought about it for a second and went for the upgrade.

That hotel made more money off my stay before I walked in, and I had an incredible experience. Because it was so personalized and timely, it never felt like a pitch. It felt like a personal concierge at a hotel who already knew what I liked and exactly when to reach out.

There's demand buried in millions of guest conversations every day. Almost none of it gets captured, because until now it hasn't been practical to.

That's why we built Portals.

It's a single link for the entire stay: instructions, directions, wifi details, digital room keys, in-room controls, an agent that answers anything, and upsell offers personalized to every guest.

Your agents personalize each portal in the conversation and place the most relevant offers at the top. Guests pay in a double-tap with Apple Pay, Google Pay, Link, and more.

Portals is live in Conduit today. Really proud of the team for building a best-in-class product yet again.

commentary.text:
Every guidebook, welcome book and QR code on the fridge fixes the half of the problem that was never broken.

The pitch …

detail_evidence.source_text:
Cole Rubin

Promoted by Conduit

Every guidebook, welcome book and QR code on the fridge fixes the half of the problem that was never broken.

The pitch makes sense. Guests have questions, so give them a well-organized place to find the answers. Nicer layout, better categories, a link in the pre-arrival message.

We measured whether any of it lands. In threads where the operator had already sent the door code unprompted, before the guest asked anything, 27.4% of guests asked for it regardless. Check-in time ran 20.8%, wifi 18.4%.

That is information sitting on their phone, in a thread they already have open. If it gets missed there, a PDF will not rescue it.

Most guidebooks are organized fine. The timing is what fails. The information arrives days before anyone wants it, and when they finally do want it, finding it becomes the guest's job.

So we built the other half. Portals is our guest portal, and the AI chat lives in it. The guest asks the question the way they would say it out loud and gets an answer that knows which property they are standing in.

"What's a good dinner spot for us tonight around here."

Keep the guidebook. Just stop expecting it to answer anything.

Link in the comments.
